Question B-003-017-009.

Why the correct answer is right: The current travels to the radio and back, so a 3 m one-way run is 6 m of conductor. Number 10 gives 6 x 0.07 V = 0.42 V. That is within the 0.5 V limit, and it is the thinnest listed wire that meets the limit.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Number 14, 0.19 V per metre": Number 14 gives 6 x 0.19 V = 1.14 V, more than twice the allowed 0.5 V drop.
- sourceIndex 2: "Number 12, 0.11 V per metre": Number 12 gives 6 x 0.11 V = 0.66 V, so it still exceeds the 0.5 V limit.
- sourceIndex 3: "Number 8, 0.05 V per metre": Number 8 gives 6 x 0.05 V = 0.30 V, so it would meet the drop limit. However, it is a heavier cable than needed. In wire-gauge numbering, the minimum acceptable gauge in this context is the thinnest listed wire that still stays within the voltage-drop limit.
